question: Annex 13-B of the EU-Mercosur agreement (Articles 13.3-13.5) provides for transitional exceptions (‘grandfathering’) for a limited, explicitly defined set of EU geographical indications, which allow the continued use of the unaltered protected name by producers from Mercosur countries. These include the products Feta, Taleggio, Marsala, Grappa, Tokaj(i) and Oporto1.

However, the PDO ‘Feta’ is fundamentally different from the other products, as it is a basic food product for mass consumption, inextricably linked to Greek agricultural production and with a high risk of direct consumer deception, while the others are specialised, alcoholic or of limited consumption, with a clearly different market position.

The possibility of marketing, within the EU, products from non-EU countries under the name ‘Feta’ for seven years creates serious distortions of competition to the detriment of thousands of Greek farmers and undermines the essence of PDO protection (see Regulation (EU) No 1151/2012). In view of the above, can the Commission say: 1.
What objective criteria led to the assimilation of Feta and the above products into the exemption regime?
How does the Commission assess the increased risk of misleading consumers, especially in the case of Feta?
Does the Commission intend to review or further limit the exemption for Feta, taking into account the disproportionate impact on the Greek agricultural economy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.3.2026) The provisions of the EU-Mercosur Partnership Agreement (EMPA) will not modify the current situation with regard to the use of the term ‘Feta’ within the territory of the European Union but will only regulate the use of the term ‘Feta’ within the Mercosur countries.

There is then no ‘exemption regime’ with regard to the ‘Feta’ within the EU but only a phasing out period of 7 years for the use of the term ‘Feta’ in the territory of Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay (under specific conditions also to avoid any misleading of consumers) after which the term ‘Feta’ will be fully protected.
